MODULE 9: FULL OUTLINE

FINAL BUZZER

Basketball School

## FINAL BUZZER

is our closing huddle where coaches see the players off as a group. The Final Buzzer should take no more than 5 minutes to maximize player's attention spans. There are five parts that should be covered in every Final Buzzer:

CALL IN

Players are verbally called in to huddle up and stand in a circle with all players and coaches if numbers allow (for larger groups, coaches may need to stand in front of the players).

CONNECTIONS

Players are given connections by the coaches as they join the Tip-Off (example of connections: high five, fist bump, handshake, pat on the shoulder).

COMMUNICATIONS

Players are delivered any relevant news or information for the day. This can include rules, expectations, directions to the bathroom, expectations for water break, etc.

CONCLUSION

Players are debriefed on the learnings and prepared for the end of the module.

CHEER

Players and coaches give an enthusiastic and excited cheer together! "NBA Basketball School on 3! (Location Name) on 6!"

MODULE 10: FULL OUTLINE

WARM-UP

Basketball School

FUNCTIONAL MOVEMENT EXPLORATION

10 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available space (no baskets needed)

### EQUIPMENT

None needed

### DESCRIPTION

Players will be given movements by the coach. The idea is to find as many ways to repeat the movement in a different way. This means players should not do the movement in the exact same way twice. For instance, when lunging, they may lunge at different speeds, in different directions, with various movements in-between each lunge, etc. Encourage players to be as creative as possible, using the loads as the different functional movements to explore for approximately 90 seconds at a time.

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Varied lunges
- Varied squats
- Varied crawls
- Varied hops
- Varied skips

### STAFF ROLE

- Watch players and remind them not to repeat identical movements.

### SCORING

N/A

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Functional movement

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "How else could you perform that movement?"

MODULE 10: FULL OUTLINE
WARM-UP
Basketball School

### I-ON-I BLOCK RACES
10 MIN
BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE
All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT
1 ball per player

#### DESCRIPTION
Players will begin in two lines behind the free-throw line. The first players in each line will tap their balls. The moment the balls tap; it is a race to see who can score a lay-up first inside the smile. Keep playing until one player scores.

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS
- Players can only score with their weak hand.
- Players must score on the opposite side to where they started.
- Players must complete one waist and leg wrap with the ball after the tap until they dribble for their lay-up.
- Players can't use the backboard for their lay-up.

#### SCORING
Players get 1 point each time they score first. First player to 4 points wins.

#### STAFF ROLE
- Ensure players rotate quickly.

#### KEY CONCEPTS
- Creative finishing
- Developing ball manipulation skills

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS
- "How can you explode to the rim to beat your opponent?"
